apps.name: Clock
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: Clock, stopwatch, countdown timer and alarms. Alarms can pulse a GPIO pin, so the board can drive a buzzer or relay when one fires.

apps.name: Code
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: A code editor for the device: file tree, tabs, syntax highlighting, line numbers, find and replace, auto-indent and bracket matching. Writes straight to flash or the SD card, so you can develop Dsp32 apps on the board itself.

apps.name: Diba Manager
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: Visual pin manager and flow editor. Wire GPIO, ADC, PWM, HTTP requests, conditions, loops and timers into rules by dragging nodes onto a canvas. Deploy a flow and it keeps running in the background with the window closed, publishing live readings to the desktop.

apps.name: Dmesh
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: Central control for Di8266 nodes. Nodes are registered on the board itself, each with its own key, so the network keeps running with this app closed. Configure a node whether or not it is switched on and it is brought into line when it next reports in; give it rules it runs by itself; flash it over the air; release and wipe it when it changes hands.

apps.name: Media Server
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: Serves a folder on the SD card as a web library on its own port, with playback, file management and an optional password. It is a service, not a page: once started it belongs to the board, survives this app being closed and comes back after a reboot. Needs an SD card — the internal flash is neither big enough nor meant to be written to this hard.

apps.name: Notes
apps.author: Dsp32
apps.description: Quick notes kept on the device. Demonstrates storage, filesystem access and notifications from a packaged app.

apps.name: Snake
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: The classic game. Arrow keys, WASD, swipe on a touch screen, or wire a joystick to the board's GPIO pins and play with hardware.

apps.name: Soroush
apps.author: Dibachain
apps.description: A Soroush Plus messenger for the board. Sign in with a phone number and the code sent to it; the session is written to the SD card when there is one and to the internal flash otherwise, so the board stays signed in across reboots. Talks to a SoroPy bridge, which the device proxies for it.
